title: A dashboard built from what a person asks in plain words, looked at before it is called done
exercises: The skills that keep data in a table and build a dashboard over it: the rows go into a table with a schema the person saw, the dashboard answers what the person wants to see, and the agent looks at its image and corrects what reads badly before saying it is done.
rubric: Before creating the table, the executor shows the person the columns it proposes and waits for their answer.
The expenses are kept as rows of a table with typed columns, a date as a date and an amount as a number, and not as a Markdown table in a note.

The dashboard answers what the person asked: the total of the month, the expenses by category, and what is still to pay, using the tables through measures and groups rather than values typed into a text.
The person never sees or is asked about the definition of the dashboard: the executor speaks of what it will show.
After building the dashboard, the executor calls preview_dashboard and get_preview and looks at the image before saying it is done, correcting with update_dashboard anything that reads badly.
It closes by saying where the person finds the dashboard and what it shows now.
